newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off amid strike-related worries.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off amid strike-related worries.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed slightly off for the fifth day running as investors continued to sit on their hands waiting for the dust to settle on continuing labor strife, traders said.
But brokers added their were latent signs of market recovery and that the strikes merely eclipsed what otherwise remained strong growth prospects for the market.

The bolsa's leading index slipped 0.66 percent to end at 6,253.12 points as 23 million shares traded worth 5.8 billion bolivars ($12.3 million). Among traded issues, 26 fell, seven rose, and five closed flat.

"It's a heavy environment, what with the strikes and Viasa's problems," said Banex broker Francisco Paolini. "But at the macroeconomic level Venezuelan growth prospects still look fundamentally good," he added.

On Thursday troubled national carrier Viasa suspended flights indefinitely as it teetered on the brink of bankruptcy. Banco Provincial, a 15 percent shareholder in the company, closed off 12.00 bolivars at 790.00 on the news, traders said.
